body:
Bulk repertoire preparation monopolizes the browser's singleton study worker after its caller has canceled. A worker-dependent destination can remain unusable for tens of seconds even though navigation succeeds immediately.

## Repeated application evidence

Captured merged main: `643f736b5e728c14f0abdd795eb38314d43a2ebe` (PR #185 merged). The workload is one installation's frozen read-only response: **8,268 transport lines, 250,503 prepared positions, 10 repertoires**, approximately 6.9 MB response JSON. No private study contents are included here.

The actual application, native worker, and real training-to-Games navigation were exercised in isolated disposable infrastructure. After the worker reported repertoire indexing running, the test clicked Games, observed its workspace request arriving before the index reply, and verified foreground work began only afterward. Three warmup pairs were excluded; 50 measured pairs alternated order. The baseline used an empty repertoire response and otherwise the same destination fixture.

| Navigation to usable Games | p50 | nearest-rank p95 | maximum |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Paired baseline | 122 ms | 478 ms | 1,118 ms |
| During actual-snapshot indexing | 33,424 ms | 46,312 ms | 50,164 ms |
| Paired added latency | **33,302 ms** | **46,179 ms** | **50,057 ms** |

All 50 contended observations exceeded 25 seconds. These are shared-host measurements with competing Node/Docker activity; every sample is retained. The worker ordering and paired difference support a material foreground performance defect for this installation's workload. They are not a population estimate or an attribution to the older deployed release. The direct dispatcher scaling, cancellation, invalidation, and lifecycle matrix remains in progress and will refine this issue's evidence.

Ordinary accepted-snapshot progression is distinct: a 50-review expected-move cohort constructed the index once, and native expected moves used the existing `tempo:move-to-paint` proxy. A separate real PostgreSQL review succeeded without rebuilding; its single existing phase sample recorded 338 ms persistence and 74 ms next-card readiness after confirmation. These observations do not qualify a p95 next-card objective.

## Root cause and cancellation

- [Home preparation and publication](https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/blob/643f736b5e728c14f0abdd795eb38314d43a2ebe/app/views/home_view.tsx#L554) loads, validates, adapts, and dispatches all repertoire lines before guarded publication.
- [Worker entry point](https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/blob/643f736b5e728c14f0abdd795eb38314d43a2ebe/app/lib/study.worker.ts#L11) executes each handler synchronously. Posting `running` does not yield to another request.
- [Computation](https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/blob/643f736b5e728c14f0abdd795eb38314d43a2ebe/app/lib/study-computation.ts#L86) canonicalizes every line, constructs positions, then builds memberships in one uninterrupted task.
- [Caller cancellation](https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/blob/643f736b5e728c14f0abdd795eb38314d43a2ebe/app/lib/background-study.ts#L122) deletes/rejects the pending caller but sends no cancellation message and does not terminate computation. Generation guards protect publication; they do not release capacity.

The investigation made no production changes. Passing characterization tests document the defect; they do not resolve it. The new Map lookup should not be blamed for the entire preparation cost without phase evidence: replay and position preparation precede membership construction.

## Reproduction and proposed correction

On the captured main with a comparable repertoire, enter training and wait for repertoire preparation to begin, then navigate to Games before it completes. Compare Games readiness with an empty repertoire control and inspect request IDs/running/reply ordering. Investigation harnesses, exact commands, sanitized raw samples, fixture seeds/checksums, and restricted private diagnostics are retained locally under `test-results/study-worker-contention-2026-10-11/`; no snapshot contents are published.

Evaluate one focused correction: isolate the complete bulk repertoire preparation path in an independently cancellable worker, preserving the foreground worker and its retained Builder/comparison state. Measure reply-transfer/main-thread cost before deciding whether a compact membership reply is also required. Priority-only scheduling cannot protect requests already blocked behind synchronous execution. No implementation is authorized by this investigation.

## Acceptance criteria for a separately authorized correction

- Named regular-suite regression first demonstrates the current foreground-capacity failure, then passes with the correction; retain real-worker ordering and output-parity proof.
- At representative realistic workloads, 50 paired queue/workspace/route/tactics and application navigation measurements show less than 50 ms p95 added foreground latency, with no reproducible background-caused stall above 500 ms. Report uncertainty and applicable existing budgets separately.
- Abort after confirmed start releases obsolete background capacity promptly without rejecting unrelated foreground callers or discarding retained foreground indexes.
- Three successive invalidations preserve latest-generation publication, bound obsolete work, settle canceled callers, and do not suppress authoritative diagnostics.
- Worker/runtime/decoding/protocol failure settles every active and queued caller; obsolete callbacks cannot publish; explicit retry recovers without rebuild loops.
- Ordinary reviews and queue refreshes reuse accepted evidence; unavailable evidence is never treated as empty or as false success.
- Focused browser and PostgreSQL workflow evidence plus complete applicable fresh candidate CI qualify the implementation before release.

Related: performance roadmap #29; completed lookup issue #36 and PR #185's contention review; PR #172 / #186 concern prepared-card progression and recovery and must retain their distinct ownership. This issue does not close or reopen those scopes.

## Freshness after PR172 merged

PR172 merged at12:08:55UTC into `d4dbf28da5b6e95db8da1acfd9fecd4655821296`, after the investigation baseline was captured. All eight measured worker/preparation modules and the complete Home repertoire effect are byte-identical on that refreshed main. The capacity mechanism has not changed; measurements stay pinned to the captured revision.

The new [prepared continuation](https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/blob/d4dbf28da5b6e95db8da1acfd9fecd4655821296/app/lib/prepared-review-continuation.ts) can advance a cached eligible card without waiting for queue acquisition. Our old-baseline ordinary progression observations do not qualify or contradict that newer critical path. Initial/fallback queue acquisition and worker-dependent navigation/tactics/routes retain the capacity risk. Issue186 is still open; PR191's overlapping review-settlement work remains a separate scope. No implementation or production change was made by this investigation.

comments.body: Reconciliation 2026-10-12: merged #120 (denied analysis admission yields capacity), #122 (maintenance wake coalescing), #83 (independent defensive-analysis pause), and #195 (installation-wide Study-only mode) provide relevant mitigation/isolation foundations. They do not by themselves demonstrate that cancelled bulk repertoire preparation cannot block foreground study. Keep open until representative workload/cancellation/foreground latency proof and live acceptance.

**Source-level finding (main, 2026-10-12):** `backend/app/services/postgres_queue_refresh.py:798-925` is the PostgreSQL daily-queue slice. It imports `main` at 804; study-only gating at 815-824 skips optional phases but retains eligibility, due/study admission, quarantine and projection publication; foreground waits at 827-869; bounded background transaction begins at 870. The same module also imports `main` in preparation/planning paths at 360,605,652 and references its queue membership, priority, eligibility helpers through 994. Thus study-only does not make daily-queue execution independent of the `main` module or background DB/admission. This is confirmed source coupling, **not** proof that this coupling caused the reported bulk cancellation stall. Require representative contention test and per-phase timing before classifying root cause.

**Investigation assignment:** #218 owns independent resource/worker topology, cancellation and background-saturation proofs for this issue. Existing merged mitigations are not proof of root-cause resolution. Any proposed repair must identify precise contested capacity, before/after latency and rollback. Coordinate with #217 before changing queue/review transaction ownership.

title: Bulk repertoire preparation blocks foreground study worker after cancellation
